valmiki.prompt: Maharishi Valmiki, an elderly Indian sage with a long flowing white beard and long white hair tied in a topknot, lean bare chest with a saffron cloth draped over one shoulder, saffron dhoti, a string of rudraksha beads

narada.prompt: the sage Narada, an adult youthful sage with a clean-shaven youthful face, black hair in a topknot, white dhoti and white shawl, carrying a long-necked veena
narada.notes: Ep02: add 'clean-shaven youthful face' and 'adult' — model otherwise drifts to bearded or child Narada

bharadvaja.prompt: a young disciple with a shaven head and a small tuft of hair, white dhoti, carrying folded bark-cloth garments

rama_teaser.prompt: a young prince Rama seen from behind, standing tall holding a great bow, wearing a simple crown and dhoti
rama_teaser.notes: Shown from behind; avoid stylised blue skin unless deliberately chosen

dasharatha.prompt: King Dasharatha, a dignified middle-aged Indian king with a short grey beard and moustache, ornate golden crown, gold jewellery, rich saffron and white royal garments
dasharatha.notes: Reuse verbatim; Ep02 scene 12 showed an aged king on a throne

kausalya.prompt: Queen Kausalya, a graceful Indian queen in a white and gold silk sari with a gold crown and long braided hair

sumitra.prompt: Queen Sumitra, a gentle Indian queen in a green and gold silk sari with a small gold crown

kaikeyi.prompt: Queen Kaikeyi, a striking Indian queen in a deep red and gold silk sari with an ornate gold crown

rishyashringa.prompt: the young sage Rishyashringa, slender with matted hair in a topknot, bare chest with a white sacred thread, ochre dhoti, holding a ladle over a sacred fire

vishvamitra.prompt: the sage Vishvamitra, a tall fierce ascetic with intense eyes, long dark-and-grey matted hair and beard, a deerskin over one shoulder, rudraksha beads, holding a wooden staff
vishvamitra.notes: Distinct from Valmiki (white beard, saffron). Ep04 lead.

vasishtha.prompt: the royal guru Vasishtha, a calm elderly sage with a long silver beard, white robes and a white shawl, gentle wise expression

rama_teen.prompt: a teenage prince Rama about fifteen, seen from behind, long dark hair tied back, simple dhoti and sash, a bow on his shoulder

lakshmana_teen.prompt: a teenage prince Lakshmana about fourteen, fair complexion, alert eyes, simple dhoti, carrying a bow and quiver

tataka.prompt: a huge solid black shadow silhouette of a rakshasi with wild flowing hair and glinting fangs, only two arms, no facial detail, not a goddess, no crown, no extra arms, no wings, no horns, not a dragon, not a gargoyle
tataka.notes: Shadow silhouette only. Ep05 scene 1 first take: a 'temple mural with ornaments' prompt produced a frontal four-armed crowned goddess (reads as Kali/Durga); Ep04 scene 4 drifted to Western bat-winged gargoyles. Keep the explicit negatives.
tataka.prompt_positive: a huge solid black shadow silhouette of a rakshasi with exactly two arms, wild flowing hair and glinting fangs, a smooth featureless shadowed face, bare-headed, human-shaped body

agastya.prompt: the sage Agastya, a short sturdy elderly sage with a white beard and a topknot, saffron cloth over one shoulder, holding a kamandalu water pot

maricha.prompt: a huge solid black shadow silhouette of a rakshasa with wild flowing hair and glinting fangs, a lean tall human-shaped body, only two arms, no facial detail, no crown, no extra arms, no wings, no horns, not a gargoyle, not a Western demon
maricha.prompt_positive: a huge solid black shadow silhouette of a lean tall rakshasa with exactly two arms, wild flowing hair and glinting fangs, a smooth featureless shadowed face, bare-headed, human-shaped body wrapped in a simple dark loincloth
maricha.notes: Follows the Tataka shadow rule. Lean and tall so he reads apart from Subahu; returns later as the golden deer, so keep the silhouette simple.

subahu.prompt: a huge solid black shadow silhouette of a rakshasa with wild flowing hair and glinting fangs, a broad heavy human-shaped body, only two arms, no facial detail, no crown, no extra arms, no wings, no horns, not a gargoyle, not a Western demon
subahu.prompt_positive: a huge solid black shadow silhouette of a broad heavy-shouldered rakshasa with exactly two arms, wild flowing hair and glinting fangs, a smooth featureless shadowed face, bare-headed, human-shaped body wrapped in a simple dark loincloth
subahu.notes: Follows the Tataka shadow rule. Broad and heavy so he reads apart from Maricha.

kushanabha.prompt: King Kushanabha, a dignified middle-aged Indian king with brown skin, a short black beard streaked with grey and a moustache, a simple gold crown, a gold necklace on his bare chest, a white dhoti with a saffron sash, exactly two arms
kushanabha.notes: Appears alone in the frame (rule for Ep08). Ancient Indian king, simple crown; nothing Mughal-coded.

brahmadatta.prompt: King Brahmadatta of Kampilya, a young Indian king with brown skin, long dark hair under a simple gold crown, a white flower garland over his bare chest, a saffron dhoti, exactly two arms
brahmadatta.notes: Appears alone in the frame, seen from behind, with the princesses only as a distant crowd. The cure is shown as his extended open palm and the distant crowd standing straight, never as a hand insert.

kushanabha_daughters.prompt: a distant crowd of small simple silhouettes of young Indian princesses with brown skin and long dark braided hair, each modestly dressed in a full-length sari with the end drawn over her head, each with exactly two arms, standing well apart from one another in loose rows
kushanabha_daughters.notes: The hundred daughters: always distant, small, well separated, modest saris, usually seen from behind. Ep07 lesson: crowded or overlapping figures grow extra arms. The curse is bending like reeds in the wind, never deformity.

himavan.prompt: Himavan, the king of the mountains, a tall regal elderly Indian king with brown skin, a long flowing white beard and long white hair falling to his shoulders under a tall simple gold crown shaped like three small snowy peaks, a white shawl draped over a pale blue-grey robe and a white dhoti, a gold necklace, exactly two arms
himavan.prompt_positive: Himavan, the king of the mountains, a tall regal elderly Indian king with brown skin, a long flowing white beard and long white hair falling to his shoulders under a tall simple gold crown shaped like three small snowy peaks, a white shawl draped over a pale blue-grey robe and a white dhoti, a gold necklace, exactly two arms, an ancient Indian king with snowy Himalayan peaks behind him
himavan.notes: Lord of mountains (शैलेन्द्र, VR 1.35.14). A dignified ancient Indian king, always with snowy peaks behind him; never a Western wizard, giant or Father Christmas. Draw in three-quarter view with the gesturing arm held clear of the robe and the beard (puppet rule); the beard ends above the chest so the arms stay free.

mena.prompt: Queen Mena, a graceful middle-aged Indian queen with brown skin, a gentle face, long dark braided hair under a small gold crown, a full-length deep green and gold silk sari with the end drawn over her head and shoulders, gold bangles, exactly two arms
mena.notes: Himavan's dear wife, daughter of Meru, mother of Ganga and Uma (VR 1.35.15). The text calls her सुमध्यमा and मनोज्ञा; render that only as grace and a gentle face, fully and modestly dressed. Three-quarter view, arms clear of the sari folds.

uma.prompt: Uma, a young Indian ascetic woman about eighteen with brown skin, a calm serene face with closed or lowered eyes, long dark hair gathered in a simple high topknot of matted locks, the topknot clearly visible, a plain full-length ochre cotton sari with its end draped over both shoulders, a single string of rudraksha beads, bare feet, exactly two arms
uma.notes: Himavan's younger daughter, rich in austerity (तपोधना, VR 1.35.20). Always modest and dignified, never glamorous, never sexualised. Usually seated cross-legged in meditation in side or three-quarter view, hands resting open on her knees and clear of the body. Distinct from Sita and the queens: no crown, no jewellery beyond the beads. Reviewer V5 (Ep10): the sari end lies over both shoulders and the topknot stays visible (never both a head covering and a topknot).

uma_girl.prompt: Uma as a young girl about ten with brown skin, a bright gentle face, long dark hair in a single braid, a simple ankle-length ochre cotton skirt, a long-sleeved ochre blouse and a light cream shawl over her shoulders, bare feet, exactly two arms
uma_girl.notes: Uma as Himavan's second daughter in the family scene (VR 1.35.16). Same ochre colour as the adult ascetic so the viewer links them. Stands apart from her mother with open board between them.

rudra_symbol.prompt: a calm seated ascetic silhouette of Rudra in solid dark grey chalk shadow, seen in three-quarter side view, seated cross-legged in deep meditation on a flat snowy rock, matted hair piled in a high topknot with a thin pale crescent moon resting in it, both hands resting on his knees, a smooth featureless shadowed face, exactly two arms, a tall plain trident standing upright planted in the rock beside him with open board around its three prongs
rudra_symbol.notes: Rudra is symbolic only (deity rule): a calm seated silhouette with crescent moon and trident, the trident planted in the rock and never held across the body. Never multi-armed, never a third eye, never a blue-skinned figurative portrait, nothing Western-fantasy. Uma's husband (VR 1.35.21).

ganga_light.prompt: the Ganga drawn as a river of light, a broad ribbon of rippling pale silver-white chalk water glowing softly from within, with small sparkles of light along its surface, drawn as plain flowing water
ganga_light.notes: The Ganga is always a river of light or water, never a woman (as in Ep09). Himavan's elder daughter (VR 1.35.16), the river of three paths.

devas_light.prompt: the gods shown as a loose row of five small glowing orbs of soft golden chalk light, each with a faint round halo, floating well apart from one another
devas_light.notes: The gods (सुराः, VR 1.35.17, 19) are symbolic lights, never figures. Keep the orbs well apart with open board around each, so each can move on its own.

krauncha_pair.prompt: a pair of krauncha birds, two graceful tall grey cranes with long slender necks, long thin legs, pale grey feathers with darker wing tips and a small red patch on the crown, standing close together side by side
krauncha_pair.notes: The pair on the Tamasa (VR 1.2.9-10), drawn as cranes as in C0002 scene 11. Side view, necks and heads against open board so each neck can move. The fallen male is always drawn whole, wings folded, with the wound kept out of the drawing.

brahma_light.prompt: Brahma shown only as a radiant golden lotus of soft light floating in the sky, eight broad petals glowing from within, gentle golden rays spreading outward on the dark board
brahma_light.notes: Deity rule: Brahma is a symbol of light (as in C0003 and C0005), never a figure. Keep open board around the rays so they can pulse.

fire_being.prompt: a tall slender human-shaped figure made entirely of glowing saffron and gold flame light, exactly two arms, a smooth glowing featureless face, bare-headed, a simple robe drawn in light
fire_being.notes: The radiant being who rises from the putriya fire with the vessel of payasa (VR 1.16.11-20). Symbolic light figure, as in C0003 scene 8. Arms and the vessel held clear of the body for puppetry.

astra_devas.prompt: tall slender human-shaped figures made entirely of soft glowing golden chalk light, exactly two arms each, smooth glowing featureless faces, bare heads, simple dhoti wraps drawn in light, bare shoulders, each figure marked by its own weapon emblem glowing at its chest
astra_devas.notes: The weapons in embodied form (VR 1.27). Text taken verbatim from the approved C0006 prompts. Keep the figures well apart with open board between them (Ep07 lesson: crowded figures grow extra arms).

ravana_shadow.prompt: a looming solid black shadow silhouette of a demon king's head and shoulders, ten crowned heads layered side by side in a wide row, each wearing a tall ancient Indian temple-style crown, smooth featureless shadowed faces, rising like a dark storm cloud
ravana_shadow.notes: Ravana is symbolic only: a layered ten-headed crowned silhouette, head and shoulders, with ancient Indian crowns (bible rule; Ep03 lesson). Arms stay out of the drawing so it never reads as a multi-armed deity form. Nothing Mughal-coded, nothing Western-fantasy.

ashram_sages.prompt: a few Indian sages with brown skin, dark hair in topknots and short dark beards, wearing white dhotis with white cloth over one shoulder, each with exactly two arms, standing well apart from one another
ashram_sages.notes: The Siddhashrama sages, text from the approved C0007 prompts. Always small and in the background, well apart.

rules: Brahma and deities: symbolic depiction (radiant lotus/light) unless owner approves figurative depiction
Composition: subject centred, title headroom top 12%, captions lower 25% clear
Ravana: symbolic only (Lanka fortress / looming crowned shadow). Never a multi-armed or third-eyed dark figure, which reads as a Hindu deity form (Bhairava/Kali). Ep03 lesson.
Architecture: ancient Indian (carved stone gateways, stepped shikhara towers, pillared halls). No onion domes or minarets (Mughal-era). Ep03 lesson.
Character tokens: write {id} (e.g. {vishvamitra}) in a scene `visual`; step_images expands it verbatim from characters.<id>.prompt (engine_version 2 prefers prompt_positive when present).

Long-form (format long, 16:9): main figure at about a third of the width, open board on the far side for camera drift, horizon about a third from the top, lower fifth plain board for captions. Rama's face stays hidden (three-quarter back view).

worlds._doc: Accent hues (HSV degrees) per world for the per-scene `accent` field; at most 3 hues per frame. The board always stays black. Source: docs/VIDEO_QUALITY_UPGRADE_PLAN.md §3.2
